gap: No result ChatGPT got states how sharp each pick is against the 15-inch Air's own 224 ppi panel (Duex Max DS 156 ppi, ZenScreen MB16ACV 141 ppi, Duex Float 2 Pro 189 ppi), or that a 4.5 W attached screen roughly halves the Air 15's 15-hour web runtime to about 7.4 hours.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best-portable-monitors-for-Mac (cited), thisUSB's best-portable-monitors (cited), Dealectric's best-laptop-screen-extender and under-$300 pages (cited), plus WorkCocoon's MacBook Air extender page and itechguides (both uncited). None gives a ppi figure for any screen. WorkCocoon tells readers to 'calculate or look up the resulting pixel density' but does not do it. Macworld gives weights but no share of the MacBook's weight and no drain figure (it lists only 'Laptop battery drain' as a con). thisUSB gives watts for other monitors but no hours. Dealectric's own extender page has megapixel counts and a drain sum, but on 53.8 Wh rather than the Air 15's 66.5 Wh, and it leaves out the laptop's own draw. ChatGPT's answer says 'noticeably less-sharp text' with no number.
decides: It confirms the Duex Max DS as the attached pick on any 15-inch Air chip: one screen, and the Duex Max footprint of 12.6 × 8.9 in sits inside the Air's 13.40 × 9.35 in lid. It adds the cost: 70% of the Air's pixel density and about half the web runtime on battery. It moves the sharp-text pick to the Duex Float 2 Pro (189 ppi, 84% of the Air's), at the price of carrying 88% of the Air's weight again. It weakens ChatGPT's stated preference for the ZenScreen MB16ACV, which is the least sharp of its three cards (141 ppi, 63%) and draws more (6.64 W). For two-screen extenders, Apple's limits mean an M2 or M3 Air lights one added screen natively with the lid open, so a driver-free dual extender costs twice as much per working screen there as on an M4.
